title: Signal embargo and launch staffing slate
content:
Purpose
---
This note sketches a narrow operational pattern for short windows where we want a temporary signal embargo (hold extra telemetry collection, or limit noisy alerts) + an attendant, lightweight staffing slate to watch key metrics. The goal: reduce noise and avoid premature throttles during controlled traffic ramps while keeping enough eyes to catch real regressions.

Context and when to use
---
- Use this when we expect a measured traffic shift (small burst/pilot) and the default alerting/sampling would either (a) spam SREs or (b) prematurely trigger capacity throttles.
- Not for full-scale launches or long (>72h) experiments. For large launches use the full launch runbook.
- Typical triggers: variant experiments, hotfix microdeploys, model roll-to-quantized-variant.

Embargo windows (proposed)
---
- Short embargo: 15–90 minutes after traffic shift begins. During this time, we temporarily:
  - increase alert dedup window from 5m -> 20m for non-critical latency buckets
  - lower the anomaly detection sensitivity threshold for token error spikes (only for service X)
  - reduce verbose tracing capture to 1% (from 5%) to avoid KV cache noise
- Soft embargo (for slower rollouts): 4 hours window with graduated re-enablement of instrumentation.

Telemetry guardrails (must-haves)
---
- Baseline capture (always on): 99th latency, error count, service health heartbeat, model fallback rate. These never go behind the embargo.
- Sampling adjustments (allowed under embargo): traces, debug logs, token-level diffs.
- Critical alerts that must remain live: 5xx surge, outage (service unavailable), storage/backplane errors, metric pipeline backpressure.
- Passive sampling buckets: increase sample size to 5x for user-visible latencies to ensure signal even with lower trace sampling.

Fail-safe thresholds (auto-unwind)
---
If any of the following happen during embargo, immediately cancel the embargo and escalate to Pager duty:
- sustained 5xx rate > 0.5% for 10m
- 99th percentile latency > SLO + 30% for 5m
- model fallback rate > 2% for 15m
- metric ingestion lag > 2x baseline

Staffing slate (roles & shift notes)
---
- Watcher (primary): owns timeline and decisions; first responder for signals. (Suggested: release-owner or oncall release lead).
- Telemetry lead (secondary): has direct access to metric pipelines and can toggle embargo config.
- SRE backup: should be available but not paged for low-severity noise.
- Model engineer (optional during model rollouts): monitors correctness/regression cues.

Proposed handoff cadence for a 3-hour short embargo event
---
- T-30m: final go/no-go. Confirm embargo config + roster, post in #release-ops.
- T-5m: preflight smoke run (critical endpoints).
- T+0: traffic shift begins. Watcher acknowledges.
- T+15m: quick check-in - passive checks only.
- T+45m: telemetry lead reduces sampling back toward baseline (if stable).
- T+90m: embargo fully lifted; post-event note in channel and short retro.

Comms ladder (what to broadcast and where)
---
- Preflight: short note in #release-ops with rollout link, embargo window, staff names, and one-line expected impact.
- During embargo: short hourly check-ins if event >1h; immediate report on any auto-unwind trigger.
- Post-event: publish a 1-paragraph outcome + link to metrics chart and any follow-up tickets.

Quick checklist (to paste in release PR comments)
---
- [ ] Confirm embargo window and who toggles it (Telemetry lead)
- [ ] Confirm Watcher and SRE backup are staffed
- [ ] Run preflight smoke (all critical endpoints)
- [ ] Link to dashboard and expected baseline ranges
- [ ] Add auto-unwind thresholds to the event notes
- [ ] Post preflight in #release-ops

Open questions / trade-offs
---
- Q: Do we want the ability to declare embargo on a per-customer basis (isolated customers)? A: not in this lightweight pattern; that's for Dedicated/private rollouts.
- Q: Should we automate embargo toggles via a small orchestration job? A: probably yes, but that requires a safe audit trail and a UI toggle in the Console; short-term manual toggle is fine.
- Q: How to avoid people using embargo as an excuse to skip telemetry? A: emphasize that critical metrics never go away; embargo only temp-damp incidental noise.

Action items (owners assigned)
---
- Marco: draft a small console toggle mock for embargo windows and permissions (due 2026-04-01)
- Evelyn: add a new line to telemetry runbook that documents auto-unwind thresholds (due 2026-03-24)
- Ravi: create a lightweight dashboard slice that Watcher can open in < 10s (due 2026-03-20)

Notes to self / rough ideas
---
- Could pair this with a short-lived read-only token for Watcher dashboards so we don't accidentally change retention.
- Keep embargo toggles auditable (log as a deploy-like event).
- In experiments where model outputs are being evaluated, signal embargo might make sense only for infra-level noise; keep application-level correctness traces intact.

Appendix: quick example command
---
- telemetryctl set-embargo --window 45m --dedup 20m --trace-sample 1% --owner priya@redwood.ai

(End)
